pr_title: Add macro to detect pointer overflow in buffer accesses

issue_context.title: z_mem_assert_virtual_region() tests for buffer wraparound incorrectly
issue_context.body:
Among other things, the routine kernel/include/mmu.h::z_mem_assert_virtual_region() performs a check to determine if the supplied buffer wraps around the end of memory (0xFF....FFFF). It performs this check using the following methodology ...
    (addr + size > addr)

Unfortunately, this is something that GCC silently ignores (see https://lwn.net/Articles/278137/ for additional details).

The unfortunate repercussion is that pointer overflows may subsequently occur because they were improperly not detected in the first place. This routine should use a methodology that is not silently ignored to detect such pointer overflows / buffer wraparounds.

review_comments: Naming nitpick: adjectives are better than verbs.  How about "Z_VALID_BUF_SIZE()" or somesuch?
